finding.claim: The ban endpoint calls require_admin inside try/except Exception. abort(403) raises an HTTPException, which the except catches. The handler only logs a warning and then runs do_ban(uid), so the admin check is never enforced. Any authenticated non-admin user can ban arbitrary users. The unban route (line 26) calls require_admin without a try/except, so it is correctly enforced.
finding.source: POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban from any authenticated non-admin user. The uid path parameter is attacker-chosen.
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20, the privileged ban operation.

trace.note: Route /admin/users/<uid>/ban has no other guard or decorator.
require_admin(g.user) is called; for a non-admin it runs abort(403) at line 11, which raises werkzeug HTTPException (an Exception subclass).
Handler only logs a warning (also logs the user name) and does not return or re-raise.
Execution continues to do_ban(uid) and returns ok=True.

finding.guards_checked: The only guard is require_admin, and its result is swallowed by the except. No decorator or middleware is present in the file, and no before_request hook exists. The unban route is not affected because it does not catch the exception.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) aborts with 403 for non-admins, but the call at admin.py:17 sits inside try/except Exception (16-19). The handler only logs and falls through to do_ban. No decorator, no before_request hook, no other guard.
verdict.reason: abort(403) at admin.py:11 raises an HTTPException, which `except Exception` at admin.py:18 swallows. admin.py:19 only logs, so do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 runs for any authenticated non-admin user (unban at admin.py:26 is unaffected).
